# Graph benchmark forensics

Measure a context tool honestly, at the level of individual sessions and individual token classes.
This drill exists because aggregates on this benchmark are routinely wrong in *both* directions, and
every headline that was ever withdrawn was withdrawn for a reason this checklist catches.

## The cost model — get this right first, everything else follows

**Cost is not "tokens".** Solve for per-token prices from recorded `total_cost_usd` (least squares
over cache_read / cache_creation / output, n≈30) rather than assuming. Measured on rep30:

| model | $/Mtok cache_read | cache_creation | output | **cost share** cr / cc / out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | 1.00 | 20.31 | 49.63 | 22% / 39% / 39% |
| Opus 5 | 0.50 | 10.19 | 24.73 | 26% / 38% / 36% |
| Sonnet | 0.29 | 6.33 | 14.78 | 41% / 31% / 28% |
| Haiku | 0.10 | 2.09 | 4.96 | 46% / 28% / 25% |

Two traps, both of which produced wrong conclusions:

- **"95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token COUNT, not a cost share.** Output is priced 20–50×
  higher, so it is 25–39% of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises writing LOSES money.
  Fable is the clean case: turns fell 10% and cost rose 15%, because output rose 14.7%.
- **Cost ≈ MESSAGES × context.** At a large context a message costs ~446k cache-read tokens. Count
  messages, not tool calls. (Note: parallel tool calls were not reachable in this harness — 0 of
  10,374 messages carried more than one — so "batch your calls" is un-actionable advice, and any
  prompt rule telling an agent to batch is dead weight given to both arms.)

Always report cache_read / cache_creation / output **separately**. The aggregate usd hides which
one moved, and which one moved is the finding.

## The noise floor — respect it or you will publish noise

- Same-instance spread across repeated cells: **45pt median**, tail to 335pt. One instance measured
  +404% / +97% / +69% across three configs.
- Every single-cell CI on this benchmark spans zero for the weaker models. **MDE ≈ CI width ≈ 31%
  at n=30**, so only effects ≥ ~30pt are detectable in one cell.
- **0/30 instances produce the same agent query twice** (median token overlap 0.55). Retrieval
  itself varies run to run, so any replay that fixes the query measures one sample of the input.

Rules that follow:
1. **Never score a partial cell.** A Sonnet geomean moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25.
2. **Never bucket one cell into sub-groups of 3–7 and read the differences.** That is how the
   "VERIFY-off is a −12pt lever" and "payload width costs 10.6pt" claims were produced, and both
   were retracted.
3. **Compare configs with replicates of the SAME config**, not two different configs' point
   estimates. Pooling different configs estimates "expected value across configs tried".
4. **Report bootstrap CIs, never a bare point estimate.**
5. Trust **deterministic offline replays** (re-issuing recorded queries against the binary) far
   more than single-session attributions.

## The measurement gate

A session counts only if `total_cost_usd > 0` **AND** `patch.diff` is non-empty. Drop pairs
**symmetrically** — if either arm gate-fails on an instance, the instance leaves both arms.
Otherwise a cheap gate-failure reads as a saving.

Also check before trusting any per-instance delta: `result` length, `num_turns`, and `subtype`
(`error_max_turns` sessions are right-censored, so their true cost is ≥ recorded).

## Fairness — the failure mode that has invalidated the most results

Every withdrawn headline on this benchmark came from **asymmetric prompts**, not from the tool.

- Diff the two arms' `prompt.txt` and account for **every** differing line. A "−35%" result once
  came from two extra instructions the tool arm had and the baseline did not (*"never write a
  throwaway test script"*, *"no `which`, no `ls vendor/`, no `find / -name php*`"*). Removing them
  moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%.
- Frugality clamps belong in the **shared** block or nowhere.
- A tool-side default change (ranking, payload content, a flag) is legitimate. Extra *instructions*
  to one arm are not.
- Distinguish "tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt" from "the tool's marginal value
  under one contract". Both are real questions; say which you measured.

## The drill

### 1. Verify the data before analysing it
- Confirm inputs exist: repo clones, graphs, and **`patch.diff` for every gated session**.
- Check for silent loss: a driver that skips on the session log alone will skip forever a session
  whose patch vanished. On this suite a `/private/tmp` reap destroyed 4 patches, 27 graphs and
  every packfile — and the lost instances were ones the tool won by 20+ turns, biasing *against* it.
- Keep the suite off volatile paths.

### 2. Score the cell
Per-instance paired table: usd, turns, cache_read/cache_creation/output, gate status. Then geomean
+ bootstrap CI. Then per-language, then per-instance sorted by contribution to the shortfall.

### 3. Decompose the transcripts — this is where the answers are
For each session (`~/.claude/projects/*/<session_id>.jsonl`, keyed off `cc_out.json:session_id`):

- **Phase split at the first Edit/Write.** Post-edit is typically ~65% of output and is where every
  losing instance's delta lives.
- **Per-tool token attribution.** Dedupe by `message.id`, credit each message's `output_tokens` to
  its tool. This tells you whether the delta is Edit bodies, Bash commands, or prose.
- **Count**: Edit/Write calls, distinct files touched, throwaway/repro scripts, prose length.
- **Classify every grep/find/read** the tool arm still ran (see below).

### 4. The single strongest predictor found: grep elimination
Compute `eg_greps / baseline_greps` per instance.

| greps eliminated | Haiku | Sonnet |
|---|---|---|
| >75% | **−46.1%** | — |
| 40–75% | −39.6% | −17.3% |
| <40% | +1.9% | +31.8% |

corr(grep ratio, log usd) = **+0.615 Haiku / +0.712 Sonnet**, while corr(**baseline** greps,
outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not task difficulty leaking through. **This is the metric to optimise.**

Then classify the *residual* greps to decide what to fix:

| what the grep was for | share | fix |
|---|---|---|
| finding something NEW | 38% | recall / ranking |
| searching inside a file the payload returned | 29% | payload under-delivery |
| re-finding a symbol the payload already gave | 25% | payload under-delivery |
| env / build hunting | 8% | verify-command quality |

### 5. Falsify offline before spending a cell
Recorded queries live at `results/<tag>/eg/<instance>/gq_calls.log`, emitted payloads at the same
path + `.payload`, worktrees at `replay-wt/<instance>`. Replay against the binary at **zero model
cost** and assert the change does what you claim — *and* that nothing else moved.

Replay across **every** recorded query variant, not one, because the agent rephrases every run.

### 6. Only then run a cell, and pre-register
Write the prediction and its falsification bounds to a file **before** the run. An out-of-sample
prediction that survives is worth more than ten post-hoc explanations. (Worked: Opus predicted
−0.1% from band effects fitted on cells excluding it; measured −0.5%, n=30.)

## Known results — do not re-derive these

- **≥35% is refuted, not unproven.** The favourable CI bound on total tokens is −27.8%
  (`eg-consolidated/AGENTS.md`). Independent rep30 measurement: Haiku −24.1% CI [−36.6, −8.3].
- Four models, rep30, paired: Fable +14.9%, Opus −0.5%, Sonnet +9.4%, Haiku −24.1%. **The tool
  saves on one of four.**
- Savings depend on how much the *no-tool* arm explores: pooled n=175, corr −0.238
  [−0.346, −0.134]; costs money under ~12 baseline turns, peaks ≈ −30% at 20–49, tapers above.

- When a result contradicts an earlier one, find the mechanism before believing either.
- Correct memory notes in place when they are falsified; a wrong note propagates.

  the transcripts, the harness, or the tool's source. But going deeper is the way through, not a
  licence to loosen the standard of evidence: report the interval, report what you retracted, and
  say plainly when a target is not reached.

# comp.md — AI-memory competitive landscape

> Owner: **memory-bench**. Compiled 2026-08-07 from a 7-agent research sweep + an adversarial
> source-check pass (15 corrections applied; wrong numbers from the raw sweep are NOT carried here).
> Companion ledger: `graph-bench-results/MemoryNotes.md`. Update in place; don't re-discover.
>
> **Number provenance tags** used throughout:
> `[self]` vendor self-reported · `[rival]` measured by a competitor (adversarial, not neutral) ·
> `[disputed]` publicly contested · `[ours-unreproduced]` our pipeline's output, not yet
> adversarially reproduced by memory-bench · **no tag = independently verified** (there are
> almost none; that is the state of this field).

---

## 0. TL;DR — the field at a glance

| System | GitHub | ~Stars | License | Domain | Headline claim | Our head-to-head status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Entire Graph (us)** | [entireio/entire-graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph) | private | — | code graph + prose memory | LOCOMO recall@10 **0.914**, QA **77.2%**; LongMemEval-S **76.0%** `[ours-unreproduced]` | — |
| **Graphify** | [Graphify-Labs/graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify) | YC S26 | — | code+docs knowledge graph | LOCOMO recall@10 0.497, QA 45.3%; LongMemEval-S 76% `[self]` | **We win both metrics in v52** (their arm scored *higher* in our harness than their own ad: 0.787/59.3%) `[ours-unreproduced]` |
| **cmm** | [DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp](https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp) | — | — | codebase intelligence MCP | 83% answer quality, 10× fewer tokens (arXiv:2603.27277) `[self]` | Off-domain on prose (see §3.3 — do NOT quote its 0.0/22.3%/6.0% as a loss). Token-side: mixed, cmm wins polyglot aggregate (TokensNotes) |
| **mem0** | [mem0ai/mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0) | 62.8k | Apache-2.0 | conversational | LoCoMo 92.5, LongMemEval 94.4, BEAM 64.1 `[self]` `[disputed]` | Not yet run in our harness |
| **Zep / Graphiti** | [getzep/graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti) (Zep proper is closed) | 29.7k | Apache-2.0 | conversational, temporal KG | DMR 94.8%; LOCOMO 75.14% `[self]` `[disputed — rival re-run says 58.44%]` | Not yet run in our harness |
| **cognee** | [topoteretes/cognee](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee) | 29.8k | Apache-2.0 | KG+vector memory | BEAM 0.79@100K/0.67@10M `[self]`; HotPotQA F1 0.840 (tuned-on-train) `[self]` | Not yet run in our harness |
| **supermemory** | [supermemoryai/supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory) | 28.8k | MIT | conversational + RAG | "95%" LongMemEval-S — **but that is Recall@15, not QA accuracy**; standard-metric figure ≈85.2–85.9 `[self]` | Not yet run in our harness |
| **Letta (MemGPT)** | [letta-ai/letta](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta) | 24.1k | Apache-2.0 | agent memory OS | DMR 93.4%; LoCoMo 74.0% *with no memory system at all* (filesystem+search agent) `[self]` | Not yet run in our harness; their filesystem result is a warning shot at the whole category (§5.4) |

**One-line read:** the conversational-memory vendors (mem0, Zep, Letta, cognee, supermemory) are in
an open benchmark knife-fight with no neutral referee; nobody in that group does codebase memory.
The code-side field is Graphify and cmm — and our v52 run beats Graphify on its own advertised
benchmarks, pending my reproduction (§3).

---

## 1. Competitors in detail

### 1.1 mem0 — [github.com/mem0ai/mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0)
- **What**: OSS "universal memory layer" for agents + hosted platform (app.mem0.ai). 62.8k★,
  Apache-2.0, Python/TS SDKs, Claude Code/Cursor skills. Conversational memory only.
- **Architecture**: LLM extraction pass (Apr 2026: single-pass ADD-only, accumulate-don't-overwrite)
  → pluggable vector store (+optional knowledge-graph variant "Mem0g") → hybrid retrieval
  (vector + BM25 + entity links + temporal ranking layer).
- **Benchmark claims** (paper: [arXiv:2504.19413](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413)):
  - LOCOMO: +26% relative on **J = LLM-as-a-Judge** vs OpenAI memory `[self]`. Paper reports F1,
    BLEU-1 *and* J; the headline is J-only (J flatters memory systems most).
  - Mem0g overall J 68.44 vs Mem0 66.88; temporal-category J 58.13 vs OpenAI 21.71 `[self]`.
  - Tokens/conv: Mem0 1,764 vs Zep 3,911 vs full-context 26,031. p95 search 0.200s `[self]`.
  - Current site ([mem0.ai/research](https://mem0.ai/research)): LoCoMo 92.5, LongMemEval 94.4,
    BEAM 64.1, ~6.9K retrieval tokens `[self]` — methodology/judge undisclosed on page.
- **⚠ The killer detail their own Table 2 shows**: **full-context beats every mem0 config on
  quality** (overall J 72.90 vs Mem0g 68.44). mem0's real pitch is cost/latency, not accuracy.
- **Disputes**: Zep rebuttal claims mem0 benchmarked a misconfigured Zep
  ([blog post](https://blog.getzep.com/lies-damn-lies-statistics-is-mem0-really-sota-in-agent-memory/));
  Letta could not reproduce mem0's MemGPT baseline and mem0 declined to clarify
  ([Letta blog](https://www.letta.com/blog/benchmarking-ai-agent-memory/)); mem0's eval prompt
  instructs the model to *never* answer "no information found" — structurally rewards
  hallucination over abstention.

### 1.2 Zep + Graphiti — [github.com/getzep/graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti)
- **What**: Zep = closed-source hosted memory platform; Graphiti = its OSS temporal-knowledge-graph
  engine (29.7k★, Apache-2.0; Neo4j/FalkorDB/Neptune backends; MCP server variant exists).
- **Architecture**: episodic ingestion → LLM entity/relation extraction → time-bounded graph edges
  (fact validity windows, never deleted — full lineage) → incremental updates → hybrid retrieval
  (vector + BM25 + graph traversal, optional anchor-node rerank).
- **Benchmark claims** ([arXiv:2501.13956](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956)):
  - DMR 94.8% vs MemGPT 93.4% `[self]`; LongMemEval accuracy +"up to 18.5%" over baseline, −90%
    latency vs full-context `[self]`.
  - **LOCOMO — the number is a live three-way dispute**: Zep originally claimed 84% (**formally
    retracted** — the post now carries a correction), self-corrected to **75.14 ±0.17**;
    mem0's independent 10-run re-run says **58.44 ±0.20**
    ([getzep/zep-papers#5](https://github.com/getzep/zep-papers/issues/5)); mem0's paper had
    separately measured an older Zep at 65.99. Quote as a disputed range, never one figure.
- **Note**: "J score" = LLM-as-a-Judge (nothing to do with Jaccard).

### 1.3 Letta (ex-MemGPT) — [github.com/letta-ai/letta](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta)
- **What**: stateful-agents platform, MemGPT lineage (24.1k★, Apache-2.0), self-host + Letta Cloud;
  also ships letta-code and [leaderboard.letta.com](https://leaderboard.letta.com).
- **Architecture**: OS metaphor — core memory (in-context editable blocks), recall memory
  (searchable full history), archival memory (vector store), agent-driven via tool calls;
  "sleep-time agents" consolidate memory between turns.
- **Benchmark claims**: DMR 93.4% (original MemGPT paper) `[self]`; Terminal-Bench 42.5%, #1
  open-source `[self]`; Letta Memory Benchmark (their own synthetic bench, model-ranking only).
- **The result that matters for everyone else**: LoCoMo **74.0% with no memory system** — raw
  transcript dumped to a file + GPT-4o-mini + filesystem search tools beat mem0's then-best 68.5%
  `[rival]` ([blog](https://www.letta.com/blog/benchmarking-ai-agent-memory/)). Their thesis:
  tool-using agents beat purpose-built memory systems. This is the same shape as our own token
  campaign's finding that harness/agent behavior dominates payload quality.

### 1.4 cognee — [github.com/topoteretes/cognee](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee)
- **What**: OSS "AI memory platform" (29.8k★, Apache-2.0, active), ECL pipeline
  (Extract→Cognify→Load) into hybrid KG+vector store; pluggable pgvector/Neo4j/SQLite/LanceDB.
- **Benchmark claims**:
  - BEAM (third-party bench, [arXiv:2510.27246](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.27246), LLM-graded):
    cognee 0.79@100K / 0.67@10M vs prior SOTA (= Hindsight) 0.735/0.641 `[self]`. Their own
    founder caveats the 10M figure as parity-within-noise, single run. (Corrected comparators:
    Honcho 63.0/40.6, RAG 32.3/24.9 — the sweep's first-pass numbers were wrong; these are from
    [Hindsight's leaderboard post](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/blog/2026/04/02/beam-sota).)
  - HotPotQA/TwoWiki/MuSiQue: large gains (F1 0.169→0.840 HotPotQA) — **tuned on train**; holdout
    drops (0.815→0.715 correctness). Their own blog: "Training-set wins are easy to fake."
  - Head-to-head (24-question HotPotQA subset): cognee-tuned 0.85 correctness vs Graphiti-default
    0.74 vs Mem0-default 0.54 `[self]` — **cognee self-discloses the asymmetry** (they tuned, the
    competitors ran default; Graphiti numbers were even reused from an older study).
- **Credit where due**: the only vendor in this list that publishes its own fairness caveats.

### 1.5 supermemory — [github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory)
- **What**: memory+context API (28.8k★, MIT), consumer app + builder API + self-host
  (`npx supermemory local`); connectors (Drive/Gmail/Notion/GitHub), OCR/video, AST-aware code
  chunking. Conversational/RAG, no code-benchmark numbers found.
- **Architecture**: chunked ingestion → fact extraction with relational versioning
  (update/extend/derive links, contradiction resolution, auto-expiry) → dual temporal grounding
  (documentDate vs eventDate) → hybrid vector+profile retrieval (~50ms profile claim).
- **Benchmark claims — metric trap, handle with tongs**: research page claims LongMemEval-S
  **"95%"** — that is **Recall@k=15, not the benchmark's QA-accuracy metric**, yet the page's
  table puts it against Zep (71.2%) and full-context (60.2%) figures. On the standard metric the
  same product reports ≈**85.86** (founder tweet) / **85.2** (as quoted by mem0's comparison
  page) `[self]` `[disputed]`. Claimed "#1 on LoCoMo and ConvoMem" — no numbers found on the
  cited page; unverified. One third-party spot-check found stale-memory failures at rough parity
  with mem0 (19/36 vs 20/36).

### 1.6 cmm (codebase-memory-mcp) — [github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp](https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp)
- **What**: single static binary; tree-sitter AST full-index of a repo (158 langs, "Hybrid LSP"
  type resolution for ~10) → persistent code knowledge graph → 14 MCP tools (search, trace,
  impact, Cypher, dead-code, cross-service HTTP links). The **code-domain** competitor.
- **Claims** `[self]`: Linux kernel (28M LOC) indexed in 3 min; <1ms structural queries; "120×
  fewer tokens"; preprint arXiv:2603.27277 — 83% answer quality / 10× fewer tokens / 2.1× fewer
  tool calls over 31 repos.
- **Our token-side history with it** (TokensNotes/graph-bench, SWE-bench-style, NOT the memory
  suite): eg beats cmm per-language on Python (3-run mean −71.4% vs −64.0%) and C; loses
  Rust/PHP/Java/Go on type resolution; **cmm wins the polyglot aggregate**. Do not conflate with
  the prose-memory results below.
- Local working clone: `graphify-parity-inputs/codebase-memory-mcp` (note: `devenv/cmm/` is a
  dangling symlink, not a checkout).

### 1.7 Graphify — [github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify)

## 2. Our status — where Entire Graph stands `[ours-unreproduced]`

### 2.1 The v52 result (the PR #84 headline)

Source bundle **on this disk**: `graphify-parity-artifacts/advertised-memory-native-v52/`
(`memory-full/REPORT.md`, `scoring/score-summary.json`, `completion-manifest.json`,
`promotion-summary.json`). Published in [entire-graph PR #84](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/84)
(OPEN, "intentionally unmerged for review").

| Benchmark | Metric | Graphify (our harness) | **Entire Graph (candidate)** | CMM diagnostic* |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LOCOMO n=300 | recall@10 | 0.7866 | **0.9143** | 0.0 |
| LOCOMO n=300 | QA accuracy | 59.33% | **77.22%** | 22.33% |
| LongMemEval-S n=50 | QA accuracy | 68.0% | **76.0%** | 6.0% |
| Graph build | LLM credits | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- n = (300 LOCOMO + 50 LongMemEval-S) × 3 reps × 3 arms = **3,150 cells**, complete
  (`completion-manifest.json` expected==observed), 0 invalid attempts, 7 retried (all recovered).
- Judge: Kimi K3 reader + Kimi K3 semantic judge, candidate answers identity-blinded; **20% Opus 5
  audit (630 cells): 98.41% agreement, kappa 0.9682**.
- Paired stat (350 cases): Entire−Graphify accuracy **+0.1648**, cluster 95% CI
  [+0.1034, +0.2146], McNemar p=1.70e-11.
- Spend: $6.25 actual API ($8.92 list); full run+scoring+audit stack $61.66 list.

**Trajectory that makes this credible as engineering (not luck)**: the earlier v45 run
([PR #83](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/83), closed as superseded) had Entire
*winning retrieval* (recall 0.918 vs 0.844) but **losing QA accuracy** (51.0% vs 67.4% LOCOMO;
44.7% vs 62.7% LongMemEval-S). The v52 prose-retrieval changes (prose-parent read windows +
additive `passages` in search output — the actual code in PR #84) are what flipped accuracy.
[PR #77](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/77) (implementation groundwork) and #83
were both closed 2026-08-07 as "Superseded by #84", branches preserved.

**Also notable**: our harness scored *Graphify itself* higher than Graphify's own advertised
numbers on LOCOMO (0.787 vs 0.497 recall; 59.3% vs 45.3% QA) — evidence the reimplementation is
not starving their arm; on LongMemEval it scored lower (68% vs advertised 76%).

### 2.2 Verification status — why every our-number carries `[ours-unreproduced]`

Per benchmark doctrine, these are my own pipeline's outputs and **have not yet been adversarially
reproduced by memory-bench** (that reproduction is my active task). PR #84 itself ships zero
reproducing bytes ("no benchmark or paid API execution performed" — numbers are pre-computed and
documented). The bundle's raw grades/manifests exist locally (path above), so reproduction is
feasible without re-spending the full run. **Do not quote §2.1 externally until the reproduction
lands in MemoryNotes.** Known open loose end: `arms.py` `GRAPH_ARMS` still lists `entire-stable`
while the v52 `score-summary.json` `memory_arms` swapped in `codebase-memory-mcp` — un-reconciled
harness-vs-artifact drift, flagged.

### 2.3 The CMM column is a diagnostic, not a defeat

cmm indexed the LOCOMO conversations into Markdown `Section` nodes, but its public
`search_graph()` BM25 path **excludes Section nodes** — it structurally cannot retrieve prose. The
0.0 recall / 22.3% / 6.0% column is an *off-domain diagnostic* (labeled so in the v52 REPORT and
PR #84) showing a code-intelligence tool doesn't transfer to prose memory — it is **not** a fair
head-to-head loss, and quoting it as one would be exactly the misconfigured-rival move Zep is
accused of (§1.2).

---

## 3. How the graphmark memory suite works

Harness: **`graphify-parity/`** package inside [entirehq/graphmark](https://github.com/entirehq/graphmark)
(private). Working copy: `devenv-worktrees/graphify-parity-prose-v52/graphify-parity/`
(CLI `graphify-parity`; key modules `graphify_parity/{arms,datasets,grading,workflows,memory_table}.py`).

**Pipeline per QA case:**

1. **Datasets** — LOCOMO (`locomo10.json`, fairness-checked for the official 1,986 raw questions)
   + LongMemEval-S cleaned (500 raw). `datasets.py:load_locomo()` L56 / `load_longmemeval()` L118
   parse sessions into `MemorySession/MemoryMessage/MemoryCase`. A sealed subsample —
   **300 LOCOMO + 50 LongMemEval-S** — is frozen once (`memory-samples.json`) and reused across
   phases; `disjoint_manifest.py` retires an inspected sample if contamination is suspected.
2. **Retrieval** — each arm's tool retrieves from its own materialized corpus: top-k=10, byte
   ceiling 128,000, identical queries/prompts/limits across arms.
3. **Reading** — a **shared Kimi K3 reader** answers from ONLY the retrieved context
   (`grading.py:448 memory_reader_messages()`, single deterministic user message).
4. **Grading** — Kimi K3 semantic judge vs reference answer (`grading.py:290`), after
   **identity-blinding** of tool-name strings (`grading.py:120 blind_candidate_answer()`;
   vocabulary sealed + hashed into `score-summary.json:identity_vocabulary_sha256`).
5. **Audit** — fixed 20% subset re-graded by Opus 5 (`opus-audit.jsonl`) → agreement % + kappa.

**Arms** (`arms.py`): `GRAPH_ARMS = (graphify, entire-stable, entire-candidate)`;
v52 release actually ran `(graphify, entire-candidate, codebase-memory-mcp)` per
`score-summary.json` (the §2.2 drift flag). 3 repetitions per phase (`phase_repetitions()`,
arms.py:35).

**Phase gate** (README ~L120-150): preflight → pilot1 (paid smoke) → tune → **holdout (untouched
10% validity gate)** → full (100%); each phase requires `verify` / `memory-score` /
`memory-report`; `promotion-summary.json` records `full_execution_basis:
"verified-holdout-validity-gate"`, status `passed`.

**Fairness controls** (README "Fairness boundary"): frozen commits for all four systems (branch +
ancestry + clean-tree checked in `config.json`); identical materialized files, queries, top-k,
byte ceiling, prompts, model IDs, repetition counts across arms; Graphify's adapter forwards only
native snippets + verified passages (no harness-synthesized source — the exact violation that
killed graphmark PR #53); Graphify runs its public `--code-only --no-cluster` path because the
public repo lacks the advertised BGE/embedding memory mode.

**Relation to graphmark proper**: graphmark's original mission is the compiler-grounded
code-intelligence benchmark (entire-graph vs cmm vs naive, scored against go/types ground truth);
the memory suite is the `graphify-parity/` layer on top. Token results live in `TokensNotes.md`;
memory results in `MemoryNotes.md`. **Never mix the two axes** — retrieval quality and token cost
have repeatedly measured as different, sometimes opposed, dimensions.

## 4. Benchmark-integrity appendix — read before quoting ANY number in this file

1. **Every headline in §1 is vendor-self-reported.** The only near-independent numbers are rivals
   measuring each other (Letta→mem0, mem0→Zep), which is adversarial, not neutral. BEAM is the
   only third-party-authored bench, but vendors self-run it.
2. **Metrics are routinely incomparable**: LOCOMO J-score (LLM-as-a-Judge), LongMemEval QA
   accuracy, BEAM composite, and supermemory's Recall@15 are four different scales. Never render
   them as one column.
3. **LOCOMO's answer key is ~6.4% wrong** (99/1540; open-domain 9.4% vs single-hop 4.3% — biases
   category comparisons), and its LLM judge accepted 63% of intentionally-wrong answers in an
   audit. 56% of per-category system comparisons are statistically indistinguishable. All LOCOMO
   numbers — including ours — inherit this.
4. **Full-context is quietly strong**: mem0's own Table 2 has full-context at the top on quality
   (J 72.90); Letta's no-memory filesystem agent at 74.0%; Hindsight notes million-token contexts
   undermine LoCoMo/LongMemEval entirely. The honest pitch for any memory system is
   cost/latency/scale, not raw accuracy — mirrors our token campaign's core finding.
5. **The Zep→84%-retraction and mem0-Zep harness fight** (§1.2) is the cautionary tale our own
   doctrine already encodes: audit the harness before believing the number, gate symmetrically,
   report CIs, publish retractions. Our v52 bundle's blinding + holdout gate + Opus audit exist
   because of exactly these failure modes — and §2 still stays `[ours-unreproduced]` until
   independently re-derived.

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any


GRAPH_ARMS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "graphify",
    "entire-stable",
    "entire-candidate",
)
CODE_ARMS: tuple[str, ...] = ("baseline", *GRAPH_ARMS)
TUNE_MEMORY_ARMS: tuple[str, ...] = ("graphify", "entire-stable")

_PROVIDERS = {
    "graphify": "graphify",
    "entire-stable": "entire-graph",
    "entire-candidate": "entire-graph",
}


def provider_for_arm(arm: str) -> str:
    try:
        return _PROVIDERS[arm]
    except KeyError as error:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown benchmark arm: {arm}") from error


def memory_arms_for_phase(phase: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if phase == "tune":
        return TUNE_MEMORY_ARMS
    if phase in {"pilot1", "holdout", "full"}:
        return GRAPH_ARMS
    raise ValueError("phase must be pilot1, tune, holdout, or full")


def phase_repetitions(
    limits: Mapping[str, Any], phase: str
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    if phase not in {"pilot1", "tune", "holdout", "full"}:
        raise ValueError("phase must be pilot1, tune, holdout, or full")
    prefix = "pilot1_" if phase == "pilot1" else ""
    memory_repetitions = limits.get(f"{prefix}memory_repetitions")
    code_repetitions = limits.get(f"{prefix}code_repetitions")
    values = (memory_repetitions, code_repetitions)
    if any(
        isinstance(value, bool) or type(value) is not int or value <= 0
        for value in values
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"sealed {phase} repetitions are malformed")
    return int(memory_repetitions), int(code_repetitions)

export const meta = {
  name: 'comp-arms-build',
  description: 'Build verified, fair memory-suite arms for mem0/zep-graphiti/letta/cognee/supermemory + BEAM 1M/10M dataset support',
  phases: [

    { title: 'Build', detail: '5 arm builders + 1 BEAM dataset agent' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'per-arm adversarial fairness/cheating verification' },
    { title: 'Integrate', detail: 'wire registration, run tests, RUN-PLAN.md with cost estimate, single commit' },
  ],
}

const WT = '/Users/suhaan/devenv-worktrees/graphify-parity-memarms/graphify-parity'
const SCRATCH = '/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/27642e0f-a981-4143-aea0-6f4f8cb34d37/scratchpad'
const COMMON = `STYLE: caveman-ultra compressed output. Use rtk where offered. Evidence = command+output or file:line.
GROUND RULES (violations have cost real money):
- Writes ONLY under ${WT} and ${SCRATCH}. NEVER touch /Users/suhaan/devenv main checkouts, the v52 worktree (graphify-parity-prose-v52), or graphmark main. No git commit/push (one integrator commits at the end).
- NO paid API keys, NO model calls, NO team-token use. Where a tool's ingestion mandates an LLM, inject a deterministic mock ONLY at the tool's own LLM-client boundary (its config/DI hook), never bypassing the tool's storage/retrieval code, and document it.
- Machine is shared with live benchmarks: pip installs go in a venv under ${SCRATCH}, docker containers get unique memarms-* names + non-default ports and MUST be stopped in smoke teardown, downloads >2GB are documented not executed.
- FAIRNESS DOCTRINE: tool OUTPUT differences are legitimate; arm-asymmetric instructions/content are not. The arm may return only what the competitor tool itself retrieved (top-k=10, byte ceiling 128000, identical query text) — no harness-synthesized source, no answer leakage, no per-arm prompt additions. The graphmark PR #53 violation (harness reading files off disk and injecting them into one arm) is the canonical cheat — never reproduce it.`

const CONTRACT_SCHEMA = { type:'object', required:['contractDoc'], properties:{
  contractDoc:{type:'string', description:'the full ARM-CONTRACT.md text (also written to disk)'},
  notes:{type:'string'} } }

const BUILD_SCHEMA = { type:'object', required:['armFile','pinnedCommit','ingestionPath','externalDeps','costDrivers','smokeOutput','deviations'], properties:{
  armFile:{type:'string'}, pinnedCommit:{type:'string', description:'competitor repo SHA pinned'},
  ingestionPath:{type:'string', description:'which of the tool s own public code paths ingestion+retrieval use'},
  externalDeps:{type:'string', description:'services/DBs/keys/models the REAL run needs'},
  costDrivers:{type:'string', description:'what the full run costs: LLM calls per conversation ingested, per query; rough token math for 300 LOCOMO + 50 LME-S + BEAM 1M/10M'},
  smokeOutput:{type:'string', description:'pasted output of the executed smoke script proving ingest+retrieve works'},
  deviations:{type:'string', description:'any deviation from the tool s default path + why; mocking points; or NONE'},
  notes:{type:'string'} } }

const VERIFY_SCHEMA = { type:'object', required:['verdict','smokeReproduced','cheatingFound','fixesRequired'], properties:{
  verdict:{type:'string', enum:['PASS','FAIL','PASS_WITH_FIXES']},
  smokeReproduced:{type:'string', description:'you re-ran the smoke yourself from a clean shell: output or failure'},
  cheatingFound:{type:'string', description:'answer leakage, synthesized content, retrieval bypass/stub, mock leaking into real path, k/byte violations, per-arm prompt asymmetry — file:line or NONE'},
  fixesRequired:{type:'string'}, notes:{type:'string'} } }

const INTEG_SCHEMA = { type:'object', required:['wired','blocked','testResults','runPlanSummary','commitSha'], properties:{
  wired:{type:'string'}, blocked:{type:'string'}, testResults:{type:'string'},
  runPlanSummary:{type:'string', description:'RUN-PLAN.md essentials: services to start, keys needed, per-arm cost estimate esp BEAM-10M ingestion, reporting format w/ tokens + latency p50'},
  commitSha:{type:'string'}, notes:{type:'string'} } }

phase('Contract')
const contract = await agent(`${COMMON}
Derive the arm-adapter contract for the graphify-parity memory suite so 5 independent builders can each add a competitor arm WITHOUT touching shared files. Read in ${WT}/graphify_parity/: arms.py, adapters.py, memory_packing.py, memory_table.py, grading.py (retrieval invocation + reader path), workflows.py (how memory arms are driven per phase), datasets.py (MemoryCase shapes), paths.py, and the v52 run config /Users/suhaan/devenv/graphify-parity-artifacts/advertised-memory-native-v52/config.json (how arms were actually parameterized).
WRITE ${WT}/ARM-CONTRACT.md containing: (1) the exact interface a new memory arm must implement (functions/classes, signatures, invocation flow file:line); (2) materialized-corpus input format the arm receives; (3) where top-k=10 and the 128000-byte ceiling are enforced and what the arm must return; (4) how registration works (arms.py GRAPH_ARMS/_PROVIDERS + adapters.py glue) — to be done by the INTEGRATOR only, builders must NOT edit those files; (5) required layout for new arms: ${WT}/graphify_parity/comp_arms/<key>_arm.py + <key>_NOTES.md + ${WT}/scripts/smoke_<key>.py; (6) how to capture per-query retrieved-token count and wall-clock latency (p50) so results can be reported on mem0-table axes; (7) the fairness invariants verbatim. Return the doc text in contractDoc.`,
  {label:'contract', phase:'Contract', schema: CONTRACT_SCHEMA, model:'opus', effort:'high'})

const CONTRACT = contract && contract.contractDoc ? contract.contractDoc.slice(0, 14000) : 'READ ' + WT + '/ARM-CONTRACT.md yourself — prior agent wrote it.'

const COMPS = [
  {key:'mem0', repo:'https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0', hint:'OSS lib mem0ai. Use its own Memory class w/ local vector store (chroma/qdrant in-process). Its LoCoMo eval harness lives in the repo (evaluation/ dir) — study it for their canonical add/search usage. Ingestion extraction is LLM-driven: mock at the LLM-client config boundary for smoke; real run needs a key (document model + call counts).'},
  {key:'graphiti', repo:'https://github.com/getzep/graphiti', hint:'Zep s OSS engine (Zep proper is closed — the arm IS graphiti and must be labeled so). Needs a graph DB: prefer FalkorDB in docker (memarms-falkordb, non-default port) or whatever its tests use lightest. Episodes API for ingestion, hybrid search for retrieval. LLM extraction: mock at its LLMClient interface for smoke.'},
  {key:'letta', repo:'https://github.com/letta-ai/letta', hint:'MemGPT lineage. Two candidate paths: (a) letta server archival/core memory APIs (sqlite dev mode if supported), (b) their letta-leaderboard LoCoMo harness (github.com/letta-ai/letta-leaderboard) which is their own published memory-bench path. Pick the one that is honestly "letta as shipped for memory recall", document the choice + rejected alternative. Mock LLM at their client boundary for smoke.'},
  {key:'cognee', repo:'https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee', hint:'ECL pipeline, self-host: sqlite+lancedb local backends documented. cognify() is LLM-driven — mock at their LLM interface for smoke. Retrieval: their search API (GRAPH_COMPLETION retriever family — but for the ARM return retrieved context only, NOT their completion answer: read the contract fairness rules; if their retriever only returns completions, use the retrieval-context layer beneath it and document).'},
  {key:'supermemory', repo:'https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory', hint:'MIT, self-host: `npx supermemory local` node server on :6767 or library path — study repo for the cleanest programmatic ingest+search without their hosted API. Bring-any-model: point extraction at a mock/local endpoint for smoke. If self-host path proves unusable offline, document exactly why + what the real run needs (their hosted API key) and build the adapter against the documented API shape with the mock server for smoke.'},
]

phase('Build')

const buildOne = c => agent(`${COMMON}
BUILD the '${c.key}' memory arm. Competitor repo: ${c.repo} — clone to ${SCRATCH}/comp/${c.key}/ and UNDERSTAND IT FULLY first (README, docs/, examples/, its own eval/benchmark code): your NOTES must prove repo understanding (cite files). Hint: ${c.hint}
ARM CONTRACT (follow exactly):\n${CONTRACT}\n
Deliverables (all under ${WT}): graphify_parity/comp_arms/${c.key}_arm.py (self-contained adapter; imports the competitor package installed in a ${SCRATCH} venv; config via env/args, no hardcoded machine paths outside documented constants); graphify_parity/comp_arms/${c.key}_NOTES.md (pinned SHA, ingestion/retrieval code paths used with file:line into the competitor repo, external deps for the REAL run, LLM cost drivers w/ token math for 300 LOCOMO convs + 50 LME-S + BEAM 1M/10M ingestion, deviations/mock points, fairness statement); scripts/smoke_${c.key}.py (tiny synthetic 3-session corpus -> ingest -> one retrieval -> print top-k passages; offline per ground rules; teardown any services). RUN the smoke and paste real output. Do NOT edit arms.py/adapters.py or any existing harness file.`,
  {label:`build:${c.key}`, phase:'Build', schema: BUILD_SCHEMA, model:'opus', effort:'high'})

const verifyOne = (b, c) => agent(`${COMMON}
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION of the '${c.key}' arm just built at ${WT}/graphify_parity/comp_arms/${c.key}_arm.py (+NOTES, +scripts/smoke_${c.key}.py). Builder's claims: pinned=${b ? String(b.pinnedCommit).slice(0,60) : '?'}; deviations=${b ? String(b.deviations).slice(0,500) : '?'}; smoke output tail=${b ? String(b.smokeOutput).slice(-600) : '?'}
Default verdict FAIL until YOU independently: (1) re-run the smoke from a clean shell and reproduce ingest+retrieve; (2) read the arm code end-to-end for cheating vectors: harness-synthesized content injected into results, answers/gold leakage, retrieval bypass (stub returning the corpus directly instead of calling the tool's search), mock leaking into the REAL path (mock must be smoke-only injection), top-k>10 or byte-ceiling violations, per-arm prompt/instruction additions, contract-interface violations vs ${WT}/ARM-CONTRACT.md; (3) trace imports to confirm the competitor's REAL retrieval code executes (not a reimplementation); (4) confirm the pinned SHA exists in ${SCRATCH}/comp/${c.key}/. ADD BEAM dataset support (mem0's table has BEAM 1M and BEAM 10M rows; we must be able to run them).   (item) => item.key === 'beam' ? beamBuild() : buildOne(item),

(4) SINGLE git commit on branch memarms/comp-arms-v1 in the worktree root (/Users/suhaan/devenv-worktrees/graphify-parity-memarms): plain conventional message, NO AI attribution footers. Do NOT push.`,
  {label:'integrate', phase:'Integrate', schema: INTEG_SCHEMA, model:'opus', effort:'high'})

Everything you asked for is now either done or building. Here's the state:

**`comp.md` is written** at `devenv/comp.md` — and mem0, zep/graphiti, letta, cognee, and supermemory were already in it (§1, one section each with GH links, stars, architecture, and every published benchmark number), alongside cmm and Graphify. Every vendor number went through an Opus source-check pass that applied 15 corrections before anything entered the doc — the notable ones: Zep's famous "84% LOCOMO" is formally *retracted* (their corrected 75.14 vs mem0's independent re-run of 58.44 is presented as the disputed range it is), supermemory's "95% LongMemEval" is a Recall@15 metric mislabeled against everyone else's QA-accuracy (~85.2 on the standard metric), and the raw sweep's "Zep uses 600K tokens/conv" was a 150× error (real: 3,911). The doc also carries our v52 status (win over Graphify on both recall and QA, explicitly tagged `[ours-unreproduced]`), a full "how the graphmark memory suite works" section (§3: datasets → sealed 300+50 sample → arm retrieval at k=10/128KB → shared Kimi K3 reader → blinded judge → 20% Opus audit → holdout gate), and a benchmark-integrity appendix.

**Competitor arms are building now** (workflow `wf_48414243-174`, 13 Opus agents, isolated worktree `graphify-parity-memarms` on branch `memarms/comp-arms-v1`): first a contract agent derives the exact adapter interface from the harness, then five builders — each required to fully study its competitor's repo — build arms for mem0, graphiti (Zep's OSS engine; Zep proper is closed-source, so the arm is honestly labeled), letta, cognee, and supermemory, plus a sixth agent adding BEAM 1M/10M from the official "Beyond a Million Tokens" dataset with its metric unmodified. Fairness is enforced structurally: each arm runs the competitor's own public code path at a pinned SHA, returns only what that tool retrieved (same k, byte ceiling, queries), and every arm gets an adversarial verifier that defaults to FAIL and re-runs the smoke itself before an integrator wires registration, runs the tests, and commits once (no push). This also covers your "dup mem0's benchmarks" ask: LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S were already in the suite, BEAM is the addition, and the contract includes capturing tokens-injected and latency-p50 so we can report on exactly mem0's table axes.

**One important gate**: all five competitors use LLM-driven ingestion, so the *full* comparison run costs real API money — BEAM-10M ingestion times five extraction-based arms is the big line. The workflow produces a `RUN-PLAN.md` with per-arm cost math; smoke tests run offline (mocks injected only at each tool's own LLM-client boundary, verified not to leak into the real path). I will not launch the paid run without showing you that estimate.

**Also in flight**: the v52 offline re-derivation (workflow `wf_0bc841c9-645`) is independently recomputing every PR #84 headline number from the raw local bundle — recall@10, QA accuracies, the +0.1648 paired CI, McNemar p, judge-agreement kappa — plus integrity checks on blinding, gate symmetry, frozen commits, and the arms-drift question. Free, zero API spend. Both workflows will report back and I'll fold verdicts into comp.md and MemoryNotes.

Earlier in this turn I also compacted the memory index (it hit its size limit) and logged all coordination in `AGENT-COMMS.md`, including the graphmark branch claim. The gcloud reauth request still stands when you get a moment.

The v52 verification is complete and the verdict is in. Summary:

**PR #84's arithmetic is fully confirmed — all 8 headline numbers reproduce bit-for-bit from the raw cells.** The Opus recompute agent never touched `score-summary.json` (the artifact under test), rebuilt every metric from the 3,150 raw grade rows, triple-sourced recall@10 with its own independent evidence-∩-hits formula (2,700/2,700 rows agree), reproduced the bootstrap CI *exactly* under the harness seed and confirmed it's stable under 4 unrelated seeds, and found the quoted McNemar p was actually the conservative choice (case-level 1.7e-11, not the smaller cell-level 9.4e-32). **But the integrity pass found four things that change how the numbers may be quoted:**

1. **The cmm arm retrieved literally nothing** — all 1,050 of its cells got the identical 24-byte empty context (zero raw hits; index builds worked, the `search_graph` BM25 retrieval is what's dead). Its 22.3%/6.0% is the reader guessing from the question alone. The bundle discloses the mechanism, but "77.2% vs 22.3%" must never be presented as a product comparison.
2. **The full 350-case headline set is not tune-disjoint** — 35 cases (10%) overlap the tune phase. The clean generalization number is the holdout: **QA 75.6%, recall 0.900** (vs full 77.2%/0.914). Small gap, but it must be quoted alongside.

4. The CI is a conversation-clustered bootstrap with effectively ~10 clusters on the LOCOMO half, and the reader and grader are the same model (kimi-k3; symmetric, with the Opus audit as mitigation).

**Bottom line: the Entire-vs-Graphify win survives** — +16.5pt QA accuracy, CI [+10.3, +21.5], with Graphify's arm cleared of any harness disadvantage (it genuinely returns fewer hits, and its reader actually got ~2× more context bytes). # /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, decide whether the loop continues.** If the task needs another iteration, call ScheduleWakeup with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks more frequent than the task needs are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.

### Correction to your premise
The RDB "freeze" was not a stall. `graphiti_arm` starts redislite with `serverconfig={"save":""}`, so `graph.rdb` is only rewritten on an explicit SAVE — file size is not a progress signal. The real signal was the embedded `redis-server` at **178% CPU with 27:51 CPU-time in 15:34 wall**. The standalone build **completed successfully** at 23:34: `{"sessions":19,"episodes":419,"nodes":1580,"edges":1161,"llm_calls":3593}` in **33 min**. Your drop criterion still fires — on wall clock, not on a hang.

### Escalation: NOT run, $0 spent
The mock-pacing hypothesis is **refuted, not untested**. Root cause found and reproduced: `redis-py` added `DEFAULT_SOCKET_TIMEOUT = 5` (`redis/_defaults.py:7`) in **8.0.0**; ≤7.4.1 defaults to `None`. Nothing in graphiti/falkordb/redislite overrides it, so every FalkorDB query got a hard 5s client deadline; `resolve_extracted_edges`'s fulltext fan-out exceeds it once the graph is large (that query alone measures 0.48s — it's concurrency, not one slow query). Pinning `redis==7.4.1` fixed it: same corpus, same binary, `8.1.0 → died at 5 min`, `7.4.1 → passed in 33 min`. A real endpoint adds ~6.2 sequential LLM round-trips per episode — strictly **slower**. So this is **not** a preflight-mock limitation and a mock-exempt variant would not recover it. `EXCLUSION.md` says exactly this.

**Projection that drove the drop:** conv-26 419 eps = 33 min measured; conv-42/43 (629/680 eps, superlinear) ≈ 50–85 min each; +LME-S ≈ 40–90 min → **2.7–4.5 h for one arm**, ~95% of preflight wall clock. ### The two original failures are both genuinely fixed
- **graphiti** — `redis==7.4.1` (above).
- **supermemory** — three separate defects, all environment-level, verified end to end (`documents_done: 19, documents_failed: 0, ingest_mode "documents"`, 10 hits / 3363 B, top hit = the gold line):
  1. the long-lived server had stopped dispatching ingest entirely (a hand-POSTed doc also stuck at `queued`); a clean `boot_sm.sh` restart fixes it — **restart before every run**;

## Root cause (file:line)

**`letta/settings.py:314`** — `disable_sqlalchemy_pooling: bool = True` is letta's *default* → **`letta/server/db.py:30-31`** sets `poolclass=NullPool`. Every ORM unit-of-work therefore opens a brand-new asyncpg connection.

Measured with a patched `BaseSelectorEventLoop.sock_connect`: **269 TCP connects to 127.0.0.1:55434 for ONE 256-passage archival insert**, 266 sockets left in `TIME-WAIT`. Under that churn a later connect never completes, and asyncpg's **default 60s** connect timeout fires at `asyncpg/connection.py:2442` (`async with compat.timeout(timeout)`).

The event loop is provably healthy during the hang — faulthandler shows the main thread idle in `selectors.select`, my loop-lag monitor never fires, `loop._selector` holds only the self-pipe fd, 2 tasks — yet `selector_events.py:651 return await fut` inside `sock_connect` never resolves. I did **not** isolate the last-mile asyncio detail (fd-reuse race is the likely candidate); the fix removes the churn, so it did not need isolating.

Two secondary findings that explain the prior agent's dead ends:
- **`db.py:44`** gates `connect_args` (including `"timeout": settings.pg_pool_timeout`) behind `if not settings.disable_sqlalchemy_pooling`. Under the default NullPool **no asyncpg connect timeout is ever configured** — which is exactly why setting `pg_pool_timeout=300` did nothing.
- 419 vs 629 is not a message threshold. Arm batch size is 256 (`letta_arm.py:291`): conv-26 → 256+163, conv-42 → 256+256+117. It is cumulative connection churn; failure lands on the second *full-size* batch. My synthetic repro: batch 1 OK in 9.65s, batch 2 dies at 62.61s.

## Fix (rung a — knobs letta already exposes)

Works without touching `letta_arm.py` because `adapters.py:266` is `env={**os.environ, **environment}` — the worker subprocess inherits `os.environ`.

```
LETTA_PG_URI=REDACTED
LETTA_DISABLE_SQLALCHEMY_POOLING=false
LETTA_PG_POOL_SIZE=5
LETTA_PG_MAX_OVERFLOW=5
LETTA_PG_POOL_TIMEOUT=60
```

- `?ssl=disable` is **required**: `db.py:52-53` forces `ssl="require"` once pooling is on unless the URI mentions ssl. Proven failure without it: `ConnectionError: PostgreSQL server at "127.0.0.1:55434" rejected SSL upgrade`.
- pool 5+5 caps it deliberately: letta's defaults (25+10) × 4 concurrent harness workers = 140 > PG `max_connections=100`.
- `LETTA_PG_POOL_TIMEOUT` drives both pool checkout (`db.py:38`) and the asyncpg connect timeout (`db.py:46`).

### 1. cognee — TWO defects (both fatal)

**(a) missing litellm routing prefix.** `LLM_MODEL=accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash` → litellm parses `accounts` as the provider → `BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided`. tenacity (`openai/adapter.py:120-126`, `wait_exponential_jitter(8,128)`) retried it 6x past the 30s `asyncio.wait_for` in `infrastructure/llm/utils.py:87-102`. **The "endpoint timed out" message was a lie** — egress was fine the whole time (`curl /models` → http=200, 0.23s).

- FIX `LLM_MODEL=openai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash`. Safe because `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` is explicitly set, so `infer_provider_from_model` (config.py:172) is skipped.

**(b) embedding engine rejects its own dimensions.** `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai` routed to `LiteLLMEmbeddingEngine`, which injects `dimensions` unconditionally (`LiteLLMEmbeddingEngine.py:177-178`) → `UnsupportedParamsError` for any non-`text-embedding-3` model.
- FIX `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai_compatible` → `OpenAICompatibleEmbeddingEngine` (direct AsyncOpenAI, never sends `dimensions`, `get_embedding_engine.py:104-113`). Model stays **bare** `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5` — that path is the SDK, not litellm.
- VERIFIED via cognee's own `test_llm_connection`: **OK 0.81s**, embed **dim=1024**.

`mem0_arm.py:300-320` passes only `{"model": ...}` for both components, so the embedder inherited `OPENAI_BASE_URL`. Measured: `embeddings.create("BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5")` on Fireworks → `BadRequestError: not available`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Raw TCP relay: listen 127.0.0.1:3129, forward every connection to api.anthropic.com:443.
TLS is passed through untouched (client verifies Anthropic's cert end-to-end)."""
import asyncio, sys

TARGET_HOST, TARGET_PORT = "api.anthropic.com", 443

async def pipe(r, w):
    try:
        while True:
            data = await r.read(65536)
            if not data:
                break
            w.write(data)
            await w.drain()
    except Exception:
        pass
    finally:
        try:
            w.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

async def handle(cr, cw):
    try:
        rr, rw = await asyncio.open_connection(TARGET_HOST, TARGET_PORT)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"upstream connect failed: {e}", flush=True)
        cw.close()
        return
    await asyncio.gather(pipe(cr, rw), pipe(rr, cw))

async def main():
    server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, "127.0.0.1", 3129)
    print("raw relay up on 127.0.0.1:3129 ->", TARGET_HOST, flush=True)
    async with server:
        await server.serve_forever()

asyncio.run(main())

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* — most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token — a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Good question — it's the central architectural split the whole benchmark is probing:

| | **Deterministic builders** (entire-graph, graphify, cmm/cmm-patched; letta is embeddings-only) | **LLM-extraction builders** (mem0, cognee, supermemory) |
|---|---|---|
| At ingestion | index the raw text mechanically — parsing, BM25, graph structure, vectors. $0, seconds | run a model over every message/chunk to *distill* it — mem0 extracts facts, cognee builds an entity graph, supermemory summarizes. ~$50 and hours for these datasets |
| What's stored | the original text, findable | a derived representation — normalized facts, linked entities |
| Where intelligence sits | **read time**: the reader model re-derives meaning from retrieved raw passages each query | **write time**: understanding is precomputed once, retrieval returns pre-digested facts |

**Does LLM-ingestion make them better? It's a bet, not a guarantee — in both directions:**

- **Where it should win**: questions needing *synthesized* knowledge — temporal reasoning ("what does she prefer *now*"), contradiction resolution, multi-hop facts scattered across sessions. A normalized fact store answers those directly; raw-text retrieval has to find and re-assemble the pieces every time. Their retrievals are also compact (fewer injected tokens).
- **Where it loses**: extraction is **lossy and fallible**. If the extractor didn't deem a detail worth saving — or distorted it — it's gone forever; the deterministic arms never lose anything because the raw text *is* the store. And the cost/latency is real: that's the hours you've been watching.
- **The standing counter-evidence**: Letta's famous result (74% on LoCoMo with *no* memory system — just an agent searching the raw transcript) and mem0's own paper showing full-context beating every mem0 config on quality. The honest pitch for extraction-based memory has always been *cost and latency at scale*, not accuracy supremacy.

That's exactly why the table reports accuracy **next to** build cost, build time, tokens injected, and retrieval latency: the LLM arms have to beat the free arms by enough accuracy to justify being ~$50 and four hours slower per corpus set. Whether they do — for the first time under one sealed harness with everyone in the room — is what lands tonight.

## Root cause

`graphify_parity/comp_arms/supermemory_arm.py:96-97`

```python

if sdk_path and sdk_path not in sys.path:

`SUPERMEMORY_SDK_PATH` = `…/smvenv/lib/**python3.14**/site-packages`; the harness interpreter is **python3.11.15**. So this put a foreign-interpreter site-packages *ahead* of the harness's own for the whole process.

My manual repro of the exact grader call under the identical env stack = 200 OK, and my manual run of the scorer's exact cmd got PAST networking. Hypothesis: IPv6-first connect attempt with no v6 route, no v4 fallback in that code path — check getaddrinfo behavior/urlopen fallback and whether a two-strike coincidence is plausible; if real, the fix may be as small as forcing v4 resolution for the client or a retry-on-101 (note models.py has max_retries — did 101 exhaust them in 1s? errno 101 fails instantly per attempt).

Establish from evidence: file mtime vs manifest write time, the trailing lines' timestamps/content (whose samples are they — the phase's resource_monitor thread finishing late? the failed score attempts appending? your pool's telemetry?), and whether v52/earlier phases had the same race (their scoring passed — what changed: your pool's thread timing? monitor shutdown ordering at raw_complete?). REPAIR at the honest layer: if it's monitor-thread-past-manifest, the harness fix is to stop/flush the monitor BEFORE manifest computation (or exclude the still-open telemetry file from the sealed manifest by design, if that's the intent elsewhere — check how preflight/v52 treated it). CRITICAL: whatever the fix, it must provably close the race for holdout AND full phase-ends, not just pilot. Also wire your Layer-1 conclusion in the same commit if it's a real code fix. ## Layer 2 — the blocker: scoring was writing into a sealed raw artifact

Not a monitor-shutdown race at `raw_complete`, and not my pool. **`memory-score` starts its own `ResourceMonitor` pointed at the raw phase's `resource-telemetry.jsonl`** (`memory_table_scoring.py:613-614` primary, `:714-715` audit) — the same file the phase seals into `artifacts.sha256.json`, and the same file scoring re-verifies at `:485-495` before doing anything else.

Evidence:

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| `artifacts.sha256.json` mtime | 23:04:08.994 |
| `resource-telemetry.jsonl` mtime | 23:06:34.774 — **the instant score run 1 exited** |
| telemetry segments | lines 1–695 `elapsed 0 → 10435.4 s` (the phase), then lines **696–706 restarting at `0.0001 → 138.8 s`** |

Two monitor instances in one file; the second span (138.8 s) matches score run 1's lifetime (23:04:11→23:06:34 = 143 s) exactly.

```
phase end    write resource-telemetry.jsonl ─┐
                                             ├─ seal artifacts.sha256.json  (23:04:08)
score run 1  verify manifest ......... OK    │
             start monitor → APPEND ─────────┘   ← pollutes the sealed file
             die (network, layer 1)              ← never reaches the end-of-scoring re-seal
score run 2  verify manifest ......... sha256 mismatch, exit 1s
score run N  identical, forever
```

**A transient failure became unrecoverable.** It never bit before because scoring had always succeeded first try, and success re-seals the manifest on the way out (`:906`), hiding the pollution. At holdout that costs ~8 h to clear; at full, days.

**Fix:** scoring writes `scoring/resource-telemetry.jsonl` — sealed normally by the end-of-scoring rewrite, bound into the completion manifest, declared in `_MEMORY_CHECKPOINT_PATHS` so the `allowed_scoring_paths ⊆ checkpoint_paths` gate still holds. No evidence lost. Raw telemetry is evidence of the raw phase and is now immutable once it ends.

Repointing two monitors fixes today's bug; **`assert_not_sealed_by_raw_manifest` closes the class** — any scoring writer aimed at a path the raw manifest sealed fails loudly at the write, for every phase and any writer added later. That is the part that provably covers holdout and full, not just pilot. No sealed artifact was hand-edited.

## Layer 1 — real code fix, not just transient

`models.py:13` imported **only** `HTTPError`; the request loop's only handlers were `HTTPError` (`:409`) and `TimeoutError` (`:448`). A bare `URLError` had **no handler**, so it escaped on attempt 1 — `max_retries=2` never applied. That is why it died in ~1 s: ENETUNREACH is instant, with no slow timeout to absorb it.

Your IPv6 hypothesis is confirmed as the trigger: the box has **no global IPv6 address and no IPv6 default route** (`ip -6 addr show scope global` and `ip -6 route show default` both empty), while `api.fireworks.ai` returns **two AAAA records beside one A record** (Cloudflare). `socket.create_connection` does fall back across a mixed answer — but a briefly cached **v6-only** answer leaves nothing to fall back to, which fits two instant failures 7 minutes apart and your later manual 200.

Fixed both halves: `URLError` is now retried like `TimeoutError`, audited as `provider_status_class="network-error"`, and placed **below** the `HTTPError` branch (HTTPError subclasses URLError — a test pins that ordering so HTTP statuses are never reclassified). Retry alone can't outlast a cached v6-only answer (3 instant attempts burn in ~3 s), so `apply_ipv4_preference_if_requested()` drops AAAA **only when the same lookup also returned an A record** — self-limiting, can never empty a working lookup on a genuinely v6-only host — opt-in via `GRAPHIFY_PARITY_FORCE_IPV4`, enabled in `run.env` with the evidence.

## Tests / state

10 new tests (`test_scoring_does_not_poison_raw.py`, `test_fireworks_network_errors.py`), written against the phase-independent mechanism — including the actual regression (failed score leaves raw artifacts verifiable), the old mechanism pinned so it can't return by another route, the guard, retry counts at `max_retries` 2 and 0, HTTPError non-reclassification, and the IPv4 filter's self-limiting behaviour. **Full suite 542 passed, 2 skipped.**

One thing I'd flag for later, unrelated to these two: `memory_table_scoring.py:828` writes `build_llm_credits = {product: 0 …}` for **every** arm, including the LLM-gated competitors — a false zero in a sealed artifact that `build_credit_evidence` deliberately avoids. ## The 2 cognee RuntimeErrors

Both are cognee's **own internal probe**: `LLM connection test timed out after 30s` (conv-49 at 02:11:58, conv-50 at 02:12:33) — its 30 s startup check failing under 8-way load, at ~30–40 s, **before any ingestion**. Not corpus defects, and a different class from the 600 s subprocess timeouts.

**Retry verdict:** one retry, only when a build fails inside `build_retry_max_elapsed_seconds` (120 s). Adapters wipe per-corpus state at the start of a cold build, so a retry restarts clean and cannot double-ingest or merge into a half-written store — the cap is what keeps it honest, guaranteeing a long, expensive, genuinely stretched build is never paid for twice. No blanket retry-on-timeout.

**Workers stay 8/24.** cognee's worst observed build is 309.8 s against a 600 s limit — it died of corpus size (full holdout conversations vs pilot ones), not contention. 3600 s gives 12x headroom either way.
