# LoCoMo — final field table

**Status: DRAFT, in flight.** Four arms still running (ETA 16:30–18:20 UTC, 2026-08-14).
Rows marked `PENDING` are placeholders and must not be quoted until filled.

---

## The measurement spine (identical for every arm)

| knob | value | why it is fair |
|---|---|---|
| answerer | **`gpt-5.6-sol`** (Azure AI) | same model answers for every system |
| judge | **`gpt-5.6-sol`** (Azure AI) | same model grades every system |
| retrieval budget | `top_k = 200` | every system asked for the same number of memories |
| dataset | LoCoMo, **n = 1540** | all questions, no subsetting |
| ingest model (LLM-extraction arms only) | `gpt-5.6-terra` | entire-graph uses **0 LLM calls** at ingest — native to each system |
| fairness guard | `FAIR_MODE=1` | hard-exits on arm-asymmetric settings |
| scoring source | aggregate `metrics_by_cutoff.top_200` | never a hand-tallied subset |

**Gate:** a run is void if drops exceed 1%, or if zero-context retrievals cluster by conversation.
Every published row below is drops = 0 unless stated.

---

## 1. Headline — same-window paired trio (drift-free)

These three ran **concurrently in one window** (`plan_g`), on the same 1540 questions.
This is the only comparison here that is immune to measurement drift.

| # | system | LoCoMo (n=1540) | vs mem0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **entire-graph — multi-resolution** | **94.68** | **+0.91** |
| 2 | mem0 OSS | 93.77 | — |
| 3 | entire-graph — previous default (one hit per file) | 92.14 | −1.63 |

Paired vs mem0: **+0.91pp, p = 0.141** — a point-estimate lead that does **not** clear
significance. Reported as such.
Paired multi-resolution vs previous default: **+2.53pp, p = 1.1e-5** — significant.

---

## 2. Full field

Cross-window rows are flagged. Same-system drift on this harness has been **measured at
2.21pp across 26h**, which is larger than the spread between the top three arms — so a
cross-window gap under ~2pp is not a reliable ordering.

| system | LoCoMo (n=1540) | window | ingest LLM calls | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **entire-graph (multi-resolution)** | **94.68** | plan_g | **0** | ships as default; `--single-resolution` opts out |
| mem0 OSS | 93.77 | plan_g | per-memory extraction | 93.44 in the `field` window — see §4 |
| cognee | 92.86 | field ⚠ | per-memory extraction | cross-window vs the trio |
| entire-graph (previous default) | 92.14 | plan_g | **0** | one result per file |
| graphify | PENDING | full | — | live |
| cmm | PENDING | full | — | live |
| letta | 80.58 | field ⚠ | per-memory extraction | cross-window |
| supermemory | 77.60 | field ⚠ | hosted | cross-window |
| graphiti | **—** | — | — | not run to completion — see §3 |
| mem0 Pro / managed | **—** | — | — | not runnable on this spine — see §3 |

---

## 3. Why a row is a dash

**graphiti — —**
Ingest cost **4,463 s per conversation history**. It completed **3 of 10** conversations
(589 of 1540 questions) before the run was stopped; roughly **160 hours** of ingest remained.
Excluded on **runtime**, not on score. Its partial figure is deliberately withheld: a partial
over 3 of 10 conversations is not comparable to a full n=1540 row, and publishing it either way
would mislead.

**mem0 Pro / managed — —**
Hosted service with no self-host path, so the answerer and judge cannot be pinned to
`gpt-5.6-sol`. Vendor-published LoCoMo figures use a different answerer and a different judge
and are therefore **not comparable** to any number in this table. Quoting them beside these
rows would be a category error, in either direction.

---

## 4. Disclosures

- **mem0 has two valid post-fix scores**: **93.77** (`plan_g`, the window shared with the eg
  arms — used in §1) and **93.44** (`field` window). Same system, same config, 0.33pp apart.
  The higher one is published against us. This is drift, not a defect.
- **mem0's original 87.40 is withdrawn.** Its adapter passed `limit`, but the library signature
  is `search(query, *, top_k=20, **kwargs)`, so `limit` was absorbed into `**kwargs` and every
  search silently returned 20 memories instead of 200. Fixed; the arm gained **6.04pp**. The
  competitor's score went **up** because of a bug we found and fixed on their side.
- **cognee's original 79.09 is withdrawn** — empty-buffer defect (state on disk, retrieval
  buffer in memory, so a resumed run searched nothing). Fixed; re-ran to 92.86.
- **Judge-failure audit:** across five audited arms, rows with an empty judge reason were
  essentially all cases where the *answerer* returned nothing, not failed judgments miscounted
  as wrong answers. Correlation between judge-failure rate and retrieved-context size across
  arms: **r ≈ 0.07**. Ranking is unchanged after excluding those rows. Re-audit of the `plan_g`
  trio (which contains the highest-context arm) PENDING.
- **Where entire-graph wins outright:** ingest speed and ingest LLM cost. eg performs **zero**

## The situation

both wrong          50
discordant          78  -> chi2=2.167, p~0.14   NOT SIGNIFICANT
```
The 0.91pp lead is a real point estimate but does not clear significance. Adding questions is impossible — LoCoMo is capped at 1540. The only way to a defensible margin is to **convert some of eg's 32 losses**.

## Your task: per-loser forensics on those 32 questions

Read-only on the VM. SSH via the live ControlMaster:
`ssh -o ControlPath=/tmp/egcm-g4.sock -o BatchMode=yes dummy '<cmd>'`
(fallback: `gcloud compute ssh graphbench-g --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '...'`)

Per-question JSON schema:
```
question_id, category, category_name, question, ground_truth_answer, evidence,
retrieval: {search_query, search_results:[{memory, score, id}], total_results, search_dropped},
cutoff_results.top_200: {judgment, score, generated_answer, memories_evaluated, reason}
```

1. Compute the exact 32 question_ids where mem0 judgment==CORRECT and eg judgment==WRONG. Also compute the 50 both-wrong for context.
2. For EACH of the 32, classify the failure by reading eg's `retrieval.search_results` against the question's `evidence` (the gold evidence turn ids). Assign exactly one primary class:
   - **RETRIEVAL MISS** — the gold evidence is not present anywhere in eg's 200 returned memories. (eg's fault, retrieval)
   - **RANK BURIAL** — gold evidence IS present but ranked low / drowned among 200 units.
   - **SYNTHESIS** — gold evidence present and well-ranked, but `generated_answer` is still wrong (the answerer failed to reason over it).
   - **JUDGE ARTIFACT** — `generated_answer` is in fact correct/equivalent to `ground_truth_answer` and the judge is wrong. Quote both strings.
   - **BAD GOLD** — the ground truth itself is wrong or ambiguous given the conversation.
   Report the count per class. This distribution is the whole deliverable — it says whether the remaining gap is even addressable by retrieval at all.
3. For the RETRIEVAL MISS and RANK BURIAL sets specifically, find what mem0 did differently: what did mem0 return that eg didn't? Is there a structural pattern (question category, evidence spread across many sessions, temporal/date reasoning, speaker attribution, counting/aggregation)?

Any fix you propose must be a **generic, question-blind mechanism**. It must NOT key off LoCoMo vocabulary, question phrasing, category labels, or anything derivable only from having seen this benchmark. A code review already caught hardcoded LoCoMo query terms (`rearrang\w*`, `organi[sz]\w*`) in `internal/sem/search_preference.go:99,318` — that is precisely the failure mode to avoid, and it is disqualifying. The test for any proposal: *would this change be justifiable in the changelog to a user who has never heard of LoCoMo?* If no, do not propose it.

Also: propose nothing that increases eg's retrieved-context byte budget much beyond its current 46.8k chars/question. mem0 uses 36.1k at the same top_k=200. An oracle arm (`plan_f_ceil`, `EG_FULL_CONTEXT=1`, `fair_mode=False`) reaches 96.23 with 100.5k chars — that arm is DISQUALIFIED and must never be published. Winning by buying a 3x context budget is not winning.

## Deliver

- class distribution table over the 32 (and over the 46 wins)
- the structural pattern behind RETRIEVAL MISS + RANK BURIAL, with question_ids as evidence
- **the single highest-yield generic fix**, with: expected conversions out of 32, expected risk to the 46, and why it is question-blind
- your honest estimate of whether the remaining gap is addressable AT ALL by retrieval. If the 32 are mostly SYNTHESIS or JUDGE ARTIFACT, say so plainly — that is a legitimate and important finding, and "the gap is not retrieval-addressable" is a fully acceptable answer. Do not manufacture a fix to have something to report.

Do NOT modify anything. Do NOT touch `$HOME/mem0harness/results/locomo/predicted_{mrq_*,full_graphify,full_cmm,mrp_*}` — those are live runs.

input.prompt:
CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED OUTPUT. Use rtk. Dense facts only.

## Goal
Produce a **same-window mem0 control** so the new entire-graph binary (`mrq_mres`, currently ~95.4 and rising, ETA 18:06 UTC) can be compared to mem0 **drift-free** on LoCoMo n=1540.

VM `graphbench-g` (zone `us-east1-b`), harness `$HOME/mem0harness`. SSH:
`ssh -o ControlPath=/tmp/egcm-g4.sock -o BatchMode=yes dummy '<cmd>'`

## Why this is delicate — read before doing anything

mem0's LoCoMo **ingest costs ~1,452 s per conversation × 10 ≈ 4 hours**. We have ~3 hours. So a from-scratch mem0 run does not fit.

BUT mem0 is **server-backed**, not in-process: containers `fieldmem0-mem0-1` + `fieldmem0-qdrant-1` have been up 23 hours, and Qdrant persists vectors on disk. If the memories from the earlier `plan_g_mem0` run (n=1540, scored 93.7662) are still resident, we can re-run **answering only** in the current window and get a genuine same-window control for free.

**THE DANGER, and it is the important part.** This project has already been burned twice by exactly this defect class: state on disk but retrieval buffer empty in memory, so a resumed run silently searched *nothing* and produced a confidently wrong score. It corrupted 500+ answers, and it destroyed cognee's number (79.09, later 92.86 once fixed). Here the failure mode is worse than usual, because **an empty mem0 store makes mem0 look terrible, which makes US look better.** A bug that flatters us is the one we are least likely to catch and the most damaging if published. Assume it is happening until you have proven it is not.

## Task

**STEP 1 — prove the store is alive. Do not skip, do not infer.**
- Query Qdrant directly (`http://localhost:6333` or whatever port `fieldmem0-qdrant-1` exposes — check `docker port`): list collections, and get the **exact vector count** per collection.
- Cross-check that count against what `plan_g_mem0` ingested (its `_ingestion_*.json` checkpoints live in `$HOME/archive_plan_harness/results/locomo/predicted_plan_g_mem0/`). Do the numbers correspond to 10 LoCoMo conversations, or is the collection empty/partial/from some other run?
- Issue a **real search** through the mem0 API at `http://localhost:18888` with `top_k=200`, using an actual LoCoMo question taken from a `plan_g_mem0` result file. Confirm it returns **200 non-empty memories**, and that they are topically plausible for that question — not 0, not 3, not generic filler.
- Confirm the answerer/judge spine still resolves: `gpt-5.6-sol` via `azure_ai` (creds in `$HOME/.azenv`).

**If ANY of these fail, STOP and report "no same-window mem0 control available".** That is a perfectly good outcome — we already have a clean drift-free trio from the `plan_g` window. Do not attempt a partial or from-scratch ingest to salvage it; a half-ingested mem0 arm is far worse than no arm.

**STEP 2 — only if Step 1 fully passes.** Launch mem0 answering-only over the same 1540 questions, concurrent with the live `mrq_*` arms:
```
--provider azure_ai --answerer-model gpt-5.6-sol --judge-model gpt-5.6-sol
--top-k 200 --top-k-cutoffs 200,50,20,10
--max-workers 3 --question-workers 10 --rpm 60      (LLM_TIMEOUT=600 in env)
FAIR_MODE=1   MEM0_HOST=http://localhost:18888
--project-name sw_mem0
```
`benchmarks/locomo/run.py` has `--resume` and `--run-id` for reusing checkpoints. Whatever mechanism you use to skip re-ingest, **verify empirically after ~30 answered questions** that retrieval is returning ~200 memories per question and accuracy is in the plausible 90s — not near zero. If accuracy is anomalously low, KILL IT IMMEDIATELY and report; do not let a broken mem0 arm run to completion and pollute the table.

Do NOT disturb the live runs: `mrq_base`, `mrq_mres`, `full_graphify`, `full_cmm`. Never overwrite a script in place while sessions run (bash reads lazily — deploy to a temp path and atomic `mv`). One process per `--project-name`; verify with `ps` before and after launch.

## Report
- Qdrant collection names + exact vector counts, and whether they match `plan_g_mem0`'s ingest
- the raw smoke-search result (how many memories, and are they plausible)
- GO or NO-GO, with the evidence that decided it
- if GO: PID, project name, and live accuracy at n≈30 and n≈100
- if NO-GO: exactly what was missing

Deadline: this must be launched by ~17:15 UTC to finish by 19:45. If Step 1 verification runs long, report NO-GO rather than launching something unverified late.

**Option B — but your version of B has a fatal statistical flaw, and fixing it is cheap. Then ALSO launch C in parallel.**

## The flaw: B as described measures regression to the mean, not your fix

The 32 losses were **selected because eg got them wrong**. Re-run those same questions with *any* binary — including an unmodified one — and a chunk will flip to correct from run-level noise alone. This project has already measured that effect: selected winners dropped by a median of 109 points on re-run. Scoring a selected subset against its own prior result is not a measurement, it is regression to the mean wearing a lab coat.

**The fix: run the subset as a YOKED PAIR, in the same window.**
- arm 1: `~/bin/eg-mr2` (contiguity + dedup)
- arm 2: `~/bin/eg-mr` (the UNCHANGED current binary) — the control
- both on the identical question list, launched together, same window

Conversions attributable to the fix = (mr2 flips to correct) − (mr control flips to correct). The control absorbs the RTM. Without it the result is uninterpretable and I will not publish it. This roughly doubles subset cost — still ~50 min total, still inside the window.

**Question list:** the 78 discordant + your 200 both-correct control (the both-correct set is the regression detector — that is where a fix like this would silently break things). Freeze the list to a file before launching so both arms provably see identical questions, and report its md5.

## Do C as well, in parallel

Launch the full n=1540 `eg-mr2` at the same time. Landing ~20:20 is 35 minutes past my target, and I would rather hand over a late definitive number than an on-time provisional one. The subset pair answers the causal question by ~19:00; the full run confirms it afterwards. Report both.

Load is fine: `mrq_base`/`mrq_mres` finish ~18:06 and free two slots. Keep every arm at `--question-workers 10 --rpm 60`, `LLM_TIMEOUT=600`.

## On your Option A — I take the point, and this is how we honour it

You are right that shipping an unverified retrieval change into a headline is how the withdrawn headlines happened, and I am not doing that. Concretely: **the published field table will NOT contain `eg-mr2` unless its full n=1540 run completes and passes the gates.** The headline stands on completed runs only. The subset pair is a decision input for me, not a table row, and it will be labelled as such.

## The design is approved

Byte-**negative** (43.4k vs 46.8k) with coverage up and breadth unchanged is exactly right, and "never return the same text twice" plus "a paragraph without its neighbours is semantically incomplete" are both justifiable to someone who has never heard of this benchmark. Take r=2. Do not chase r=3/r=4 for +1/+2 conversions — you would be spending the byte headroom that makes the change unimpeachable.

Your point that the design never reads the query is the single most important fairness property here. **State it explicitly in the PR description and in the code comment**: this is a post-ranking assembly rule that cannot key off any benchmark because it never sees a question.

Take the time you need for `mise run check` green — do not rush the `SearchResponse.Validate` invariants on non-overlapping source-ordered passages. A broken merge that trips validation in production is far worse than a late number. Message me the moment `~/bin/eg-mr2` exists.

## What

Ranking returns **one region per file**. That is correct for code, where a file is the unit
you want to open. It is wrong for prose, where a single markdown document can hold the answer
across several distant regions.

The extra regions **already exist**. `search_prose_parent.go` plans them and
`search_prose_passage.go` attaches them to their parent as `Passages` — but a consumer reading
`results[]` never sees them. Measured on a real prose corpus, search returned 19 results across
19 files while carrying **195 passages holding 42 KB of evidence that no `results[]` consumer
could reach**; ranks 6–19 got a one-line snippet.

When fewer distinct files match than `--top-k` asked for, this change spends the spare slots
promoting those regions to results of their own.

## Why it cannot regress code search

- Strictly additive: runs **after** selection, only fills slots the distinct-file ranking left
  empty (`len(results) >= topK` → no-op), so it can never displace a file.
- Never breaches `--max-context-bytes`.
- No code result carries passages, so code search has nothing to promote.

Verified empirically: 16 real code queries against this repo at `--top-k 10` **and** `--top-k 50`,
full JSON compared — **0 mismatches**.

`--single-resolution` restores the previous output.

## Verification

Measured on LoCoMo (n=1540 per arm), paired and same-window, **both arms on the identical
corpus with only the binary differing** — answerer and judge both `gpt-5.6-sol`, `top_k=200`.

| | previous | this change | Δ | discordant | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all pairs (n=634 so far) | 91.91 | 94.06 | **+2.16pp** | 16 / 4 | **0.012** |

The estimate has held in the **+2.2 to +2.5pp** band across ten reads from n=118 upward. The
full n=1540 run is still completing; this PR should not merge until it lands and passes the
gates.

Mechanism check — the change fires and does what it claims:

```
shipped binary : 17.60 units/q across 17.60 distinct files  -> ratio 1.00
this change    : 40.22 units/q across 17.60 distinct files  -> ratio 2.29  (same files)
```

The control arm was verified **byte-identical to the shipped binary** across 45 queries × 3
corpora (full JSON, latency/cache stats stripped, 0 mismatches), so the measured delta is
attributable to this change alone.

It is also not a context dump: 30–40% of corpus bytes returned, against the previous 22–29%.

## Fairness

This is a **post-ranking assembly rule that never reads the query**. It cannot key off any
benchmark, because it never sees a question. No question-conditioned branching, no vocabulary
lists, no category logic.

# LoCoMo — memory system comparison

**entire-graph is first on accuracy and first on ingest speed, with zero LLM calls at ingest.**

Every system: all **1,540** LoCoMo questions. Answerer **and** judge are both `gpt-5.6-sol`
(Azure AI) for every arm. Retrieval budget `top_k = 200` for every arm. Identical questions,
identical source conversations. Zero dropped questions anywhere.

| # | system | LoCoMo | ingest LLM calls | ingest, full dataset | search latency | context returned |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **entire-graph** | **94.68** | **0** | **17m 46s** | 868 ms | 46,602 ch |
| 2 | mem0 OSS | 93.77 | 1+ per memory | 55m 25s | 535 ms | 35,960 ch |
| 3 | cognee | 92.86 | 1+ per memory | 14h 17m | 7,585 ms | 82,077 ch |
| 4 | cmm | 91.30 | 0 | 24m 26s | **22 ms** | 36,756 ch |
| 5 | graphify | 87.34 | 0 | 23m 22s | 194 ms | 16,213 ch |
| 6 | letta | 80.58 | 1+ per memory | 4h 42m | 5,848 ms | 10,276 ch |
| 7 | supermemory | 77.60 | hosted | 5h 52m | 8,014 ms | 7,418 ch |
| — | graphiti | — | 1+ per memory | **~12h+** (did not finish) | — | — |
| — | mem0 Pro / managed | — | hosted | — | — | — |

### Accuracy by question type

| system | single-hop | multi-hop | temporal | open-domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **entire-graph** | **95.4** | **89.7** | **92.5** | **79.2** |
| cmm | 93.6 | 91.8 | 90.7 | 71.9 |
| graphify | 92.3 | 81.9 | 83.2 | 74.0 |

*(n = 841 / 282 / 321 / 96)*

---

## What the speed numbers mean

**Ingest is where the gap is structural.** entire-graph indexes the entire LoCoMo dataset in
**under 18 minutes with zero LLM calls**. cognee needs **14 hours and 17 minutes** — 48× longer —
because it calls an LLM to extract facts from every chunk. supermemory takes 5h 52m, letta 4h 42m,
mem0 55m. entire-graph is the fastest ingest of every system measured, and the only one in the
top three that costs nothing in tokens to build.

That difference compounds: LLM-extraction systems pay again on every update, and their ingest
cost scales with corpus size and with model pricing. A deterministic index does not.

**Search latency is the one axis where entire-graph is not first.** cmm answers in 22 ms and
graphify in 194 ms, against entire-graph's 868 ms; mem0 is faster too at 535 ms. Multi-resolution
retrieval is what raised this — the previous entire-graph default searched in 252 ms and scored
92.14. We spent roughly 600 ms per query to buy 2.5 accuracy points. Against the LLM answer
generation that follows every search, that is not a user-visible cost, but it is a real
regression and it is stated rather than hidden.

**Context returned** is what each system puts in its 200 slots. entire-graph is mid-range:
cognee returns **76% more** context than entire-graph and still scores lower, so the ranking is
not explained by prompt size.

---

## Why two systems have no score

**graphiti** — ingest costs 4,463 seconds per conversation. It completed 3 of 10 conversations
with roughly 160 hours of ingest remaining, and was stopped. Excluded on runtime, not on quality.
Its partial result is withheld because 3-of-10 is not comparable to a full run.

**mem0 Pro / managed** — a hosted service with no self-host path, so its answerer and judge cannot
be pinned to `gpt-5.6-sol`. Vendor-published figures use a different answerer and a different
judge and are not comparable to this table in either direction.

---

## Three competitors scored higher because we fixed their bugs

Every defect below was found by us, in a competitor, and every fix **raised that competitor's
score**:

- **mem0 +6.04 points** (87.40 → 93.77). Its adapter passed `limit` to `search()`, whose signature
  is `search(query, *, top_k=20, **kwargs)`. `limit` was swallowed by `**kwargs`, so every search
  silently returned 20 memories instead of 200.
- **cognee +13.77 points** (79.09 → 92.86). State was written to disk while the retrieval buffer
  lived in memory, so a resumed run searched nothing and scored confidently wrong answers.
- **cmm — from structurally zero to 91.30.** Shipped v0.9.0 excludes `Section` nodes from its own
  BM25 result set (`src/mcp/mcp.c::bm25_search`), so a prose corpus returns
  `{"total":0,"results":[]}`. The published score uses a one-line fix removing that exclusion and
  changing nothing else. Reported in cmm's favour.

---

## Method

- **Answerer and judge:** `gpt-5.6-sol` (Azure AI) for every system, no exceptions.
- **Retrieval budget:** `top_k = 200` for every system.
- **Ingest:** native to each system. entire-graph, cmm and graphify use no LLM. Extraction-based
  systems use `azure_ai/gpt-5.6-terra`.
- **Scoring:** taken only from each run's aggregate `metrics_by_cutoff.top_200`, never a
  hand-tallied subset.
- **Gate:** a run is void if dropped questions exceed 1%, or if empty-context retrievals cluster
  by conversation. Every published row has **zero** drops and **zero** empty-context retrievals.
- **Fairness guard:** `FAIR_MODE=1` hard-exits on any arm-asymmetric setting.
- **Ingest timings** are wall-clock for all ten conversations on a 32-core `c4-standard-32`,
  measured from the runs' own completion timestamps.
- **Hardware:** GCP `c4-standard-32`, us-east1-b.

Runs were not all executed simultaneously. Where two systems are within ~2 points of each other

# Pre-registration — LoCoMo headline claim

**Written 2026-08-14 17:02 UTC, while the deciding runs are at ~56% and ~27% complete and the
final numbers are unknown.** The point of writing it now is that the decision rule cannot be
chosen after seeing which rule flatters us.

Live state at time of writing: `mrq_mres` 862/1540, `sw_mem0` 414/1540. Last read of the
primary endpoint: eg 95.41 vs mem0 93.48, +1.93pp, discordant 12–4, p = 0.0768.

---

## Primary endpoint (one, fixed)

**Paired McNemar, entire-graph (`mrq_mres`) vs mem0 OSS (`sw_mem0`), same window, all 1540
LoCoMo questions, ALL-PAIRS.**

Same window means both arms answered concurrently against the same endpoint, so measurement
drift — which has been observed at 2.21pp on this harness across 26h — applies to both equally.

Reported always, whatever the value: point estimate, discordant split (gain/loss), exact
McNemar p, and a bootstrap CI.

## Decision rule — committed in advance

| outcome | what we publish |
|---|---|
| **p < 0.05** | "entire-graph beats mem0 on LoCoMo, +Xpp, significant (p = X, n = 1540, paired)." |
| **0.05 ≤ p < 0.10** | "entire-graph leads mem0 by Xpp. This does **not** reach conventional significance (p = X)." The lead is stated as a point estimate and is **not** called significant. |
| **p ≥ 0.10** | "entire-graph and mem0 are **statistically tied** on LoCoMo accuracy; the point estimate favours entire-graph by Xpp." |

In every branch, the accuracy result sits beside the two findings that do not depend on it:
**entire-graph is first on ingest speed and is the only top-three system with zero LLM calls at
ingest.** Those are structural, not statistical, and they do not need a p-value.

## What we will NOT do after seeing the number

- **No switching to the judge-gated figure to obtain a better p.** Judge-gated is reported
  beside the primary as a secondary, always, in every branch.
- **No switching cutoff** (`top_50` / `top_20` / `top_10`) to find a better result. `top_200` is
  the registered budget.
- **No post-hoc question exclusions.** The only exclusions permitted are the gates fixed in
  advance: drops > 1%, or empty-context clusters by conversation, applied symmetrically.
- **No sub-category headline.** Per-category cells (n ≈ 96–841) are descriptive only; they lack
  the power to support a claim, and the discordant counts inside them are single digits.
- **No replicate-until-significant.** One run per arm.

## Secondary, reported regardless

- The banked `plan_g` window: eg 94.68 vs mem0 93.77, **+0.91pp, discordant 46/32, p ≈ 0.14** —
  a point-estimate lead that does not clear significance. Published as such.
- The product change: `mrq_mres` vs `mrq_base`, same window, same corpus, binary the only
  difference.

## Known risk, stated in advance

At n = 414 the discordant split is 12–4. Discordant counts are precisely where early splits are
least stable: 12–4 can become 20–14 by n = 1540 and land back above 0.05. That is an expected
outcome, not a failure, and the table above already says what we publish if it happens.

## A fix that was built, measured, and rejected

The obvious remedy — expanding retrieved fragments to their contiguous neighbours, paid for by
deduplicating text already returned — was implemented and measured against all 32 losing
questions:

```
                  chars/question    gold evidence turns found
control                 44,532            21 / 51
with the fix            44,484            23 / 51
```

**+2 evidence turns, all within a single question.** One conversion in 32, moving p from 0.14
to at best 0.12. It does not clear its own bar and is **not shipped**.

An earlier build of it appeared to convert more — while growing retrieved text **+90%**. The
byte ceiling had been placed on the serialized JSON payload, where a ~1,560-byte envelope dwarfs
a ~150-byte snippet, so dropping duplicate results "freed" envelope that does not exist as text.
Re-bounded on the text a consumer actually reads, the gain vanished. The diagnosis behind it is
unaffected and stands: perfect session-level recall, turn-level miss, 70% of missing gold within
two turns of already-retrieved text. **The fix fails on economics, not on premise** — there is
not enough duplicate text to pay for the widening, and taking the budget from anywhere else is
buying the result with a bigger prompt.

## STEP 1 — solve the matching problem FIRST, and report your method before any numbers

`evidence` holds gold ids; `search_results[].memory` holds text. You must establish a defensible way to decide whether a returned memory *contains* a gold evidence item. **Report the exact schema of `evidence` (inspect real files) and your matching rule before producing any table.**

Prior art from another agent that worked: LoCoMo unit ids encode session + turn index, so gold turn ids can be resolved to their text via the source dataset and matched against returned memory text. Find the source conversations on the VM (the corpora the arms ingested) and use them to resolve gold ids to gold text.

**The matching rule must be arm-neutral.** Systems return different unit types — mem0 returns ~200 extracted per-turn memories, cognee returns **1 unit of ~82,000 chars**, graphify returns ~98 graph nodes, entire-graph returns ~199 fragments. A rule like "exact string equality" would score cognee at zero purely because it returns one big blob, and a rule tuned to fragments would flatter entire-graph. **Substring/containment matching on normalised text is likely correct precisely because it is agnostic to unit size** — but justify whatever you choose, and state explicitly which arms it could bias and in which direction. 4. **Evidence density** — gold items found per 1,000 characters returned. This is the efficiency measure: cognee returns 82k chars per question, entire-graph 46k, graphify 16k, so raw recall alone rewards whoever dumps the most text.
5. **The decomposition that matters:** cross-tabulate recall against correctness —

| **cmm** | markdown Section node | **438** | SQL `select label,count(*) from nodes` on `full_cmm/.../mem-*.db` → Section=438 |

## Verdict: YES — and worse than hypothesized

entire-graph's default is **the coarsest indexing of any arm**, by a wide margin.

- vs mem0: **16.4x coarser** (19 vs 312)
- vs cmm / graphify: **23–24x coarser** (19 vs 438 / 457)
- vs supermemory / graphiti: **22x coarser** (19 vs 419)

# FAIRNESS VERDICT

**FOR is correct on the principle. AGAINST is correct about the instrument. They do not conflict, because the env var is not the only way to satisfy FOR.**

The FOR case is stronger than stated. Every competitor picks its own granularity, and none picked session: mem0 312, cmm 438, graphify 457, supermemory 419. Holding entire-graph to 19 is not a neutral default, it is a 16–24x handicap that caps the arm at 19 evidence items while every rival draws 200. It is the same class of defect as the three competitor bugs repaired in their favour — an arm that cannot use the top-k the harness grants it is misconfigured, not outperformed.

The AGAINST case is also correct, and decisive against *the env var specifically*. `EG_INGEST_GRANULARITY=turn+session` lives in `benchmarks/common/entire_client.py`, not in the product. It rewrites the corpus before entire-graph ever sees it. A user who installs entire-graph today and points it at their notes gets 19 documents and 19 results. Publishing the env-var number reproduces the trap already caught once.

**Verdict: granularity parity is the right fair setting; `EG_INGEST_GRANULARITY` is the wrong way to obtain it.** The publishable configuration is `mrq_mres` — shipped corpus shape, product binary, 195 items. It clears the handicap using code that is on a branch and default-on, so the claim is "entire-graph with PR #100 does this", which a user can reproduce by installing that build. `sw_eg_tsmr` is a **mechanism probe**, not a headline: it isolates whether ingest-side splitting adds anything once retrieval-side multi-resolution exists. If it lands at or near `mrq_mres`, that is the strongest possible result — it proves the harness lever is redundant and the product change is doing the whole job.

Cite the headline off `mrq_mres` vs `sw_mem0`. Cite `sw_eg_tsmr` only as evidence about the mechanism.

It is a real product change, and **it is already written**. The worktree at `/Users/suhaan/devenv/eg-multires` (branch `feat/prose-context-expansion`) carries two commits:

- `fccf1fc` **feat(search): multi-resolution prose retrieval** — 386 insertions, one new file `internal/sem/search_multi_resolution.go` plus hooks in `search.go`/`cli`. When fewer distinct files match than `--top-k` asked for, the spare slots promote the extra regions the ranker *already computed* and currently discards as unread `passages`. Strictly additive, runs after selection, never breaches `--max-context-bytes`, cannot displace a file. Code search is untouched because no code result carries passages. `--single-resolution` restores old behaviour.
- `8a28407` **feat(search): assemble prose context instead of returning fragments** — 557 insertions, `internal/sem/search_prose_context.go`. Cross-document verbatim dedup, plus ±2-paragraph widening capped at 40 lines, holding snippet bytes constant against the pre-assembly total. Both rules are query-blind. Opt out with `--no-context-expansion`.

**Size: ~943 insertions, 2 new files, 3 files touched, ~468 lines of tests.** Both default-on. **No ingest-time change of any kind** — no multi-granularity document splitting, no re-indexing, no corpus format change, no migration. That is the elegant part: the coarseness was never in the index, it was in the ranker returning one region per file, and the finer regions were already being computed and thrown away.

Status: **PR #100, open, not merged.** Merging it is what converts the benchmark number from config-conditional to genuine. That is the single blocking action, and the honest framing of the result is:

> entire-graph's shipped ranker returns one region per file — correct for code, wrong for prose. On LoCoMo that capped it at 19 evidence items per conversation against every competitor's 200. PR #100 spends the unused top-k slots on regions the ranker already computed, lifting it to ~195 with no ingest change, and closes the gap to mem0.

The dedup that was starving is now sitting on the largest possible source of duplication, and the freed budget is exactly what pays to keep session context beside turn precision.

**18:18 UTC — we found why entire-graph loses multi-hop, and it's a one-line design flaw.**

**`selectSearchCandidates` admits one candidate per *file*.** The 438 markdown section regions **exist in the graph and are scored** — then collapsed to 19. PR #100 promotes some back, but as *satellites*: they inherit the parent's score verbatim (`Score: parent.Score`) and are appended after every parent, so they can never outrank one.

**The artifact proof:** 200 returned results carry exactly **19 distinct scores**. 181 of 200 are score-duplicates of one of 19 parents.

**And here's the consequence nobody had connected.** The harness sorts memories by score with a *stable* sort. With 19 distinct scores, the list collapses into 19 blocks — session-1's parent plus its ~9 passages, then session-2's block, and so on. **At the top-50/20/10 cutoffs the answerer only ever sees the top one or two sessions.** Multi-hop questions require stitching fragments *across* sessions — structurally impossible. That is our single largest deficit against mem0 (−1.44), explained.

**The fix, already implemented — the prose retrieval unit becomes the section, not the file:**

| | items/q | distinct regions | chars/q |
|---|---|---|---|
| current + PR #100 | 198.7 | **19** | 69.6k |
| pre-split corpus (harness flag) | 200.0 | 200 | — |
| **`eg-mr3`, default corpus** | **200.0** | **200** | **53.0k** |

Full region diversity **from the shipped corpus**, with **24% fewer bytes** — because ~9.5k chars per question were being computed and discarded unread. No ingest change, no harness flag, byte-negative. That's the shippable version of the configuration that was winning.

**Meanwhile, as predicted:** the stacked arm's lead is decaying on schedule — +2.65 at n=718, now **+1.05 at n=859**. I'm not quoting it until 1540.

**The plan when the binary lands:** `eg-mr3` at default granularity, full n=1540, launched **concurrently with a fresh mem0 control** so it's same-window. The bar is mem0's **94.22**.

The one thing that could block it: `selectSearchCandidates` is shared by code and prose, so unlike PR #100 this is **not** structurally inert for code search. That needs real evidence, and I've made it the gating item.
